chunks: And what is in it from Isa ibn Abi Mansur, I have narrated it from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan - may Allah be pleased with him - from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn ibn Abi Al-Khattab, from Jafar ibn Bashir, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Isa ibn Abi Mansur - and his kunya was Abu Salih, and he was Kufan and a mawla - and we were narrated by Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan - may Allah be pleased with him - from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Saffar, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd Al-Hamid, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Ibn Abi Yafur, who said:

I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when Isa ibn Abi Mansur approached, and he (the Imam) said to me: 'If you want to see the best in this world and the best in the hereafter, then look at him.'

key_terms.أَبُو صَالِحٍ: Abu Salih, the kunya (honorific name) of Isa ibn Abi Mansur
key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الدُّنْيَا: The world, referring to worldly life and conduct
key_terms.الْآخِرَةُ: The Hereafter, referring to the afterlife and eternal life
key_terms.عِيسَىٰ بْنُ أَبِي مَنصُورٍ: Isa ibn Abi Mansur, a prominent companion of the Imams

ai.seo_question: Who is Isa ibn Abi Mansur and why did the Imam recommend looking at him?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the reliable chain of Shaykh al-Saduq, highlights Isa ibn Abi Mansur’s dual excellence in dunya and akhira, a distinction that underscores the Shia emphasis on the integration of spiritual piety with worldly competence. The Imam’s directive to 'look to him' serves as a practical model for the community, affirming his status as a trustworthy authority in both religious knowledge and ethical conduct during the era of the Imams.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Everything in this book that is narrated from Isa ibn Abi Mansur has been transmitted by me from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan - may Allah (swt) be pleased with him - from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn ibn Abi Al-Khattab, from Jafar ibn Bashir, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Isa ibn Abi Mansur, whose kunya was Abu Salih. He was a Kufan and a freed servant (mawla).
We were also narrated by Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan - may Allah (swt) be pleased with him - from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Saffar, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd Al-Hamid, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Ibn Abi Yafur, who said:
I was with Abu Abdullah (as) when Isa ibn Abi Mansur approached, and he (the Imam) said to me: "If you want to see the best in this world and the best in the hereafter, then look at him."
